Not a product bug in the job board: `waitForScreen('10 running')` had already passed, so all ten jobs started.

The drained wait was `waitForOutput(settleMs: 500, timeout: 60 s)` — a **silence settle** (returns once the raw buffer is unchanged for 2 consecutive 500 ms polls ≈ 1 s of stream quiet). But this scenario staggers its ten `sleep` jobs **exactly 1 s apart** (3..12 s), so the gaps *between* settle notices sit right on that threshold. One stretched inter-notice gap on the loaded runner (job 7 → 8) satisfied the silence rule and the wait **returned mid-drain** with the tail jobs unlanded — hence exactly `{1..7}`. ## Fix shape

1. **Harness primitive** (`pty_harness.dart`): new `FaCliHarness.waitForRaw(matched, {what, timeout})` — the predicate-anchored raw-stream wait, reusing the existing `pollUntil` engine: polls the accumulated raw buffer until `matched` accepts, returns the capture AT the hit, and throws `TimeoutException` with screen + raw-tail diagnostics on expiry. Available to all sibling suites.
2. **Proof predicate extracted** (`settledJobNumbers` + `shellJobSettleNotice`): top-level in the harness (the `maskedValueRow` convention — unit-testable without a PTY), keeping the existing tolerances: DISTINCT-set proof against repaint re-emits, number-prefix match against CI-load mid-id fragmentation (`sh-10-…xqo<esc>… exited(0)`).
3. **Test rewired**: the drained wait is now `waitForRaw((raw) => settledJobNumbers(raw).length == 10, timeout: 120 s)` — anchored on the proof data itself, generous CI ceiling, loud expiry. The screen-side proofs are untouched: `10 running` peak, mid-countdown photo, `0 running` drain, terminal summary card, composer-reserved rows.

## What stays proven

Unchanged contract: all ten background jobs start (board peaks at `10 running`), the count is photographed strictly between 10 and 0, **every one of the ten jobs settles** (distinct settle notices `{1..10}`), the board drains to `0 running · 10 done · 0 lost` with no live row and no foreign paint in the composer's reserved zone.

- `dart analyze` clean on the three touched files; **23/23 green** on the harness default-suite unit proofs (`pty_harness_settled_jobs_test` (new: repaint dedup, fragmentation tolerance, truncated-{1..7} rejection), `poll_until`, `masked_value_row`, `frame_content`, `fa_bin`) + the gh-1049 `pty_screen_wait_reg` guard — Dart 3.13.4 temp SDK + fleet pub cache.
- The PTY leg itself **could not run locally**: `PseudoTerminal.start` fails with `openpty failed` on this Mac (the known sibling-lane blocker; deterministic <1 s, unrelated to the scenario). Per repo policy PTY-tagged tests run in nightly + on demand, not the per-PR gate — the green per-PR legs here are the unit proofs above; the integration shard is CI's to prove.
- Deliberately NOT included: a whole-file `dart format` reflow of the countdown suite (formatter version skew would bury the ~40-line fix under 260 lines of churn; no CI format gate on this file).

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1345
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1345
- **Title**: test(1337): anchor countdown drain on the settle-notice predicate, not stream silence
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1337-pty-countdown-flake` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +118
- **Deletions**: -17
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T20:00:31Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T20:28:49Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1337

## Root cause (why the window «expired» on the slow runner)

The failing assertion is the settle-set check in `shell_job_countdown_pty_test.dart` (#573 review): expected `{1..10}`, actual `{1..7}` — job 8's settle notice (and 9, 10) missing from the capture. Not a product bug in the job board: `waitForScreen('10 running')` had already passed, so all ten jobs started.

The drained wait was `waitForOutput(settleMs: 500, timeout: 60 s)` — a **silence settle** (returns once the raw buffer is unchanged for 2 consecutive 500 ms polls ≈ 1 s of stream quiet). But this scenario staggers its ten `sleep` jobs **exactly 1 s apart** (3..12 s), so the gaps *between* settle notices sit right on that threshold. One stretched inter-notice gap on the loaded runner (job 7 → 8) satisfied the silence rule and the wait **returned mid-drain** with the tail jobs unlanded — hence exactly `{1..7}`. Aggravator: `waitForOutput` returns silently on timeout, so expiry never surfaced diagnostics; the 60 s ceiling was never even reached.

## Fix shape

1. **Harness primitive** (`pty_harness.dart`): new `FaCliHarness.waitForRaw(matched, {what, timeout})` — the predicate-anchored raw-stream wait, reusing the existing `pollUntil` engine: polls the accumulated raw buffer until `matched` accepts, returns the capture AT the hit, and throws `TimeoutException` with screen + raw-tail diagnostics on expiry. Available to all sibling suites.
2. **Proof predicate extracted** (`settledJobNumbers` + `shellJobSettleNotice`): top-level in the harness (the `maskedValueRow` convention — unit-testable without a PTY), keeping the existing tolerances: DISTINCT-set proof against repaint re-emits, number-prefix match against CI-load mid-id fragmentation (`sh-10-…xqo<esc>… exited(0)`).
3. **Test rewired**: the drained wait is now `waitForRaw((raw) => settledJobNumbers(raw).length == 10, timeout: 120 s)` — anchored on the proof data itself, generous CI ceiling, loud expiry. The screen-side proofs are untouched: `10 running` peak, mid-countdown photo, `0 running` drain, terminal summary card, composer-reserved rows.

## What stays proven

Unchanged contract: all ten background jobs start (board peaks at `10 running`), the count is photographed strictly between 10 and 0, **every one of the ten jobs settles** (distinct settle notices `{1..10}`), the board drains to `0 running · 10 done · 0 lost` with no live row and no foreign paint in the composer's reserved zone.

## Local verification (honest disclosure)

- `dart analyze` clean on the three touched files; **23/23 green** on the harness default-suite unit proofs (`pty_harness_settled_jobs_test` (new: repaint dedup, fragmentation tolerance, truncated-{1..7} rejection), `poll_until`, `masked_value_row`, `frame_content`, `fa_bin`) + the gh-1049 `pty_screen_wait_reg` guard — Dart 3.13.4 temp SDK + fleet pub cache.
- The PTY leg itself **could not run locally**: `PseudoTerminal.start` fails with `openpty failed` on this Mac (the known sibling-lane blocker; deterministic <1 s, unrelated to the scenario). Per repo policy PTY-tagged tests run in nightly + on demand, not the per-PR gate — the green per-PR legs here are the unit proofs above; the integration shard is CI's to prove.
- Deliberately NOT included: a whole-file `dart format` reflow of the countdown suite (formatter version skew would bury the ~40-line fix under 260 lines of churn; no CI format gate on this file).

Now I have all three changed files. Let me verify:

1. The diff matches the files on disk (the repo is presumably checked out at the PR HEAD).
2. Run the analysis checks that I can.
3. Consider other suites that used `_settleNotice` — did other tests use the same regex pattern that could now be consolidated? Let me grep for `settleNotice`, `exited(0)`, `waitForOutput(settleMs: 500`, and similar patterns in the repo for potential duplication the PR could have addressed (or duplication introduced).

Key review questions:

1. **Correctness of `waitForRaw`**: it delegates to `pollUntil`, polling `matched(_rawBuffer.toString())` every 50 ms with the timeout. On hit, returns `_rawBuffer.toString()`. Good — capture at hit.

2. **Regex `shellJobSettleNotice = RegExp(r'\[bash\] sh-(\S+) exited\(0\)')`**:
   - `(\S+)` is greedy. For a line like `[bash] sh-10-…xqo<esc>[11;29H5<esc>[11;31H exited(0)`, the `\S+` will match `10-…xqo\x1b[11;29H5\x1b[11;31H` — wait, are escape characters `\S`? `\x1b` (ESC) is a non-whitespace character (it's a control char but not whitespace), so yes `\S+` matches it. Then ` exited(0)` follows. So group(1) = `10-…xqo\x1b[11;29H5\x1b[11;31H`, and `.split('-').first` = `10`. OK, the fragmentation test passes.
   - But what about fragmentation BETWEEN the number and the dash? E.g. if a repaint interleaves an escape after `sh-1` and before `0`, group(1) would be `1\x1b[11;29H0...`. Then `.split('-').first` = `1\x1b[11;29H0` — wait, no. `split('-')` splits on `-`; the first token would be `1\x1b[11;29H0` — hmm, actually if escape is inserted mid-number, split('-').first returns the corrupted number token like `1<ESc>[11;29H0`, which would NOT equal `10`, inflating the distinct set with a corrupt entry. The doc says "The number is the first token written, so it survives any such fragmentation" — that assumes the fragmentation occurs after the full number is written. The observed case (`sh-10-…xqo<esc>[11;29H5<esc>[11;31H`) is mid-id (after the number and first dash). This is a pre-existing tolerance (was in the old test code too), not newly introduced. It's a known limitation documented. Not a regression. Could flag as a suggestion at most — but it's pre-existing behavior moved. Since the code was moved verbatim, this is fine.

   - Another subtlety: what if a settle notice is for a FAILED job, i.e. `exited(1)` or `lost`? The regex only matches `exited\(0\)`. The old regex was the same, so no change. But hmm — the drained wait requires exactly 10 distinct numbers with `exited(0)`. If a job fails (exited(1)), the wait would never satisfy and it'd hit the 120 s timeout, throwing with diagnostics. That's arguably correct behavior (test should fail loudly), fine for a test.

   - What about `\S+` greediness combined with multiple notices one line? E.g. `[bash] sh-1-a exited(0) [bash] sh-2-b exited(0)`. `allMatches` — after the first match consumes `1-a` (greedy `\S+` would try to match as much non-space as possible: `1-a` then ` exited(0)`). Wait — greedy `\S+` matches `1-a`, then requires ` exited\(0\)`. It works. Second match found later. But what if the raw stream contains `[bash] sh-1-a exited(0)[bash] sh-2-b exited(0)` (no space between)? Greedy `\S+` would match `1-a` and then need ` exited(0)` — ` exited(0)` present, matches `1-a`. Fine.

   - What about `exited(0)` for `sh-10-abc10 exited(0)` — greedy `\S+`: could `\S+` match `10-abc10` and then ` exited(0)` — yes. Good.

   - Edge: the number-prefix extraction `m.group(1)!.split('-').first`. If a job id fragment contains a `-` before the number (can't — id always starts `sh-N-...`). OK.

3. **`settledJobNumbers` returning a Set<String> of numbers as strings**: the test expects `{for (var i = 1; i <= 10; i++) '$i'}` — fine.

4. **Potential issue — the `waitForRaw` predicate `settledJobNumbers(raw).length == 10` counts distinct numbers GLOBALLY in the raw buffer, not just for THIS scenario's jobs.** The harness CWD is a unique temp git dir, the session is fresh per spawn, so only this scenario's jobs exist. But `settledJobNumbers` counts ANY `[bash] sh-… exited(0)` notice in the raw buffer. If some earlier part of the scenario (the boot, or the first turn) ran other bash jobs... In this test, the scripted turns only launch the ten sleep jobs. OK. But as a harness-level API (available to all sibling suites), the count-based predicate semantics are the caller's concern. Fine.

5. **The `what:` parameter default and the `timeout` default of 10 s** — consistent with `waitForText`/`waitForScreen` (which use 10 s default). Good.

6. **The `_rawBuffer` access in `waitForRaw` — `_rawBuffer.toString()` is computed on every poll iteration twice (once in matched, once onHit)**. For a long raw buffer (a 2-minute PTY session could accumulate a lot of output), `StringBuffer.toString()` is O(n) each poll — every 50 ms. `waitForText` does the same (`_rawBuffer.toString()` per poll), so consistent with existing patterns. And the predicate `settledJobNumbers(raw)` runs a regex over the entire raw buffer every 50 ms — O(n) per poll. For a 5-minute test with heavy repaints, the raw buffer could be hundreds of KB to a few MB. Running `allMatches` over it every 50 ms = 10k regex scans/s over ~1 MB → could add CPU load on the runner, slightly aggravating the very load the test suffers from. Hmm, this is worth a SUGGESTION: the predicate could track the last-checked length or the regex could be applied only to the tail. But is it a real problem? The raw buffer of a countdown session: ten jobs over ~12 s with a TUI repainting... TUI repaints can be substantial (full-frame repaints, maybe a few KB per frame). Over ~120 s at, say, 5-10 repaints/s * 2-4 KB = maybe 1-4 MB. Regex over 4 MB every 50 ms: `allMatches` with a literal-prefix regex — Dart regex will scan for `[bash] sh-` literal occurrences; ~4 MB scan is on the order of a few ms (simple literal scan is fast, maybe 1-10 ms). So per poll ~ up to 10 ms CPU every 50 ms = up to 20% of one core. Non-trivial but not fatal on a test runner; and `waitForText` already does `.contains(pattern)` per poll which is also O(n). I'll note it as a SUGGESTION (capture last-match-end / incremental scanning), not blocking.

7. **Duplication**: `_settleNotice` in the countdown test was removed and now uses the harness-level `shellJobSettleNotice`/`settledJobNumbers` — good consolidation. Are there OTHER suites that define the same regex locally (`\[bash\] sh-… exited`)? Let me grep. If other suites duplicate this pattern, the PR could have consolidated them too — but that might be scope creep; the ticket scopes to the countdown flake. Still, worth checking for at least flagging as a suggestion (or noting they intentionally left them).

8. **The new test file `pty_harness_settled_jobs_test.dart` runs in the DEFAULT suite** (no integration tag) — it imports `pty_harness.dart`. Does importing pty_harness.dart pull in `dart:io` and pty2/xterm deps into the default suite? The file itself has `@TestOn('vm')`. pty_harness.dart imports `package:pty2` and `package:xterm` — these are regular dependencies presumably available in the default suite too (the file compiles fine as the author claims 23/23 green on the default suite). Since `pty_screen_wait_reg_test.dart` also greps... the author says it runs in the default suite and is green locally. Fine.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the

  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it

The drained wait was `waitForOutput(settleMs: 500, timeout: 60 s)` — a **silence settle** (returns once the raw buffer is unchanged for 2 consecutive 500 ms polls ≈ 1 s of stream quiet). 3. **Test rewired**: the drained wait is now `waitForRaw((raw) => settledJobNumbers(raw).length == 10, timeout: 120 s)` — anchored on the proof data itself, generous CI ceiling, loud expiry. The screen-side proofs are untouched: `10 running` peak, mid-countdown photo, `0 running` drain, terminal summary card, composer-reserved rows.

## What stays proven

Unchanged contract: all ten background jobs start (board peaks at `10 running`), the count is photographed strictly between 10 and 0, **every one of the ten jobs settles** (distinct settle notices `{1..10}`), the board drains to `0 running · 10 done · 0 lost` with no live row and no foreign paint in the composer's reserved zone.

- The PTY leg itself **could not run locally**: `PseudoTerminal.start` fails with `openpty failed` on this Mac (the known sibling-lane blocker; deterministic <1 s, unrelated to the scenario). Per repo policy PTY-tagged tests run in nightly + on demand, not the per-PR gate — the green per-PR legs here are the unit proofs above; the integration shard is CI's to prove.

Now I have all three changed files. Let me verify:

1. The diff matches the files on disk (the repo is presumably checked out at the PR HEAD).
2. Run the analysis checks that I can.
3. Consider other suites that used `_settleNotice` — did other tests use the same regex pattern that could now be consolidated? Let me grep for `settleNotice`, `exited(0)`, `waitForOutput(settleMs: 500`, and similar patterns in the repo for potential duplication the PR could have addressed (or duplication introduced).

Key review questions:

1. **Correctness of `waitForRaw`**: it delegates to `pollUntil`, polling `matched(_rawBuffer.toString())` every 50 ms with the timeout. On hit, returns `_rawBuffer.toString()`. Good — capture at hit.

2. **Regex `shellJobSettleNotice = RegExp(r'\[bash\] sh-(\S+) exited\(0\)')`**:
   - `(\S+)` is greedy. For a line like `[bash] sh-10-…xqo<esc>[11;29H5<esc>[11;31H exited(0)`, the `\S+` will match `10-…xqo\x1b[11;29H5\x1b[11;31H` — wait, are escape characters `\S`? `\x1b` (ESC) is a non-whitespace character (it's a control char but not whitespace), so yes `\S+` matches it. Then ` exited(0)` follows. So group(1) = `10-…xqo\x1b[11;29H5\x1b[11;31H`, and `.split('-').first` = `10`. OK, the fragmentation test passes.
   - But what about fragmentation BETWEEN the number and the dash? E.g. if a repaint interleaves an escape after `sh-1` and before `0`, group(1) would be `1\x1b[11;29H0...`. Then `.split('-').first` = `1\x1b[11;29H0` — wait, no. `split('-')` splits on `-`; the first token would be `1\x1b[11;29H0` — hmm, actually if escape is inserted mid-number, split('-').first returns the corrupted number token like `1<ESc>[11;29H0`, which would NOT equal `10`, inflating the distinct set with a corrupt entry. The doc says "The number is the first token written, so it survives any such fragmentation" — that assumes the fragmentation occurs after the full number is written. The observed case (`sh-10-…xqo<esc>[11;29H5<esc>[11;31H`) is mid-id (after the number and first dash). This is a pre-existing tolerance (was in the old test code too), not newly introduced. It's a known limitation documented. Not a regression. Could flag as a suggestion at most — but it's pre-existing behavior moved. Since the code was moved verbatim, this is fine.

   - Another subtlety: what if a settle notice is for a FAILED job, i.e. `exited(1)` or `lost`? The regex only matches `exited\(0\)`. The old regex was the same, so no change. But hmm — the drained wait requires exactly 10 distinct numbers with `exited(0)`. If a job fails (exited(1)), the wait would never satisfy and it'd hit the 120 s timeout, throwing with diagnostics. That's arguably correct behavior (test should fail loudly), fine for a test.

   - What about `\S+` greediness combined with multiple notices one line? E.g. `[bash] sh-1-a exited(0) [bash] sh-2-b exited(0)`. `allMatches` — after the first match consumes `1-a` (greedy `\S+` would try to match as much non-space as possible: `1-a` then ` exited(0)`). Wait — greedy `\S+` matches `1-a`, then requires ` exited\(0\)`. It works. Second match found later. But what if the raw stream contains `[bash] sh-1-a exited(0)[bash] sh-2-b exited(0)` (no space between)? Greedy `\S+` would match `1-a` and then need ` exited(0)` — ` exited(0)` present, matches `1-a`. Fine.

   - What about `exited(0)` for `sh-10-abc10 exited(0)` — greedy `\S+`: could `\S+` match `10-abc10` and then ` exited(0)` — yes. Good.

   - Edge: the number-prefix extraction `m.group(1)!.split('-').first`. If a job id fragment contains a `-` before the number (can't — id always starts `sh-N-...`). OK.

3. **`settledJobNumbers` returning a Set<String> of numbers as strings**: the test expects `{for (var i = 1; i <= 10; i++) '$i'}` — fine.

4. **Potential issue — the `waitForRaw` predicate `settledJobNumbers(raw).length == 10` counts distinct numbers GLOBALLY in the raw buffer, not just for THIS scenario's jobs.** The harness CWD is a unique temp git dir, the session is fresh per spawn, so only this scenario's jobs exist. But `settledJobNumbers` counts ANY `[bash] sh-… exited(0)` notice in the raw buffer. If some earlier part of the scenario (the boot, or the first turn) ran other bash jobs... In this test, the scripted turns only launch the ten sleep jobs. OK. But as a harness-level API (available to all sibling suites), the count-based predicate semantics are the caller's concern. Fine.

5. **The `what:` parameter default and the `timeout` default of 10 s** — consistent with `waitForText`/`waitForScreen` (which use 10 s default). Good.

6. **The `_rawBuffer` access in `waitForRaw` — `_rawBuffer.toString()` is computed on every poll iteration twice (once in matched, once onHit)**. For a long raw buffer (a 2-minute PTY session could accumulate a lot of output), `StringBuffer.toString()` is O(n) each poll — every 50 ms. `waitForText` does the same (`_rawBuffer.toString()` per poll), so consistent with existing patterns. And the predicate `settledJobNumbers(raw)` runs a regex over the entire raw buffer every 50 ms — O(n) per poll. For a 5-minute test with heavy repaints, the raw buffer could be hundreds of KB to a few MB. Running `allMatches` over it every 50 ms = 10k regex scans/s over ~1 MB → could add CPU load on the runner, slightly aggravating the very load the test suffers from. Hmm, this is worth a SUGGESTION: the predicate could track the last-checked length or the regex could be applied only to the tail. But is it a real problem? The raw buffer of a countdown session: ten jobs over ~12 s with a TUI repainting... TUI repaints can be substantial (full-frame repaints, maybe a few KB per frame). Over ~120 s at, say, 5-10 repaints/s * 2-4 KB = maybe 1-4 MB. Regex over 4 MB every 50 ms: `allMatches` with a literal-prefix regex — Dart regex will scan for `[bash] sh-` literal occurrences; ~4 MB scan is on the order of a few ms (simple literal scan is fast, maybe 1-10 ms). So per poll ~ up to 10 ms CPU every 50 ms = up to 20% of one core. Non-trivial but not fatal on a test runner; and `waitForText` already does `.contains(pattern)` per poll which is also O(n). I'll note it as a SUGGESTION (capture last-match-end / incremental scanning), not blocking.

7. **Duplication**: `_settleNotice` in the countdown test was removed and now uses the harness-level `shellJobSettleNotice`/`settledJobNumbers` — good consolidation. Are there OTHER suites that define the same regex locally (`\[bash\] sh-… exited`)? Let me grep. If other suites duplicate this pattern, the PR could have consolidated them too — but that might be scope creep; the ticket scopes to the countdown flake. Still, worth checking for at least flagging as a suggestion (or noting they intentionally left them).

8. **The new test file `pty_harness_settled_jobs_test.dart` runs in the DEFAULT suite** (no integration tag) — it imports `pty_harness.dart`. Does importing pty_harness.dart pull in `dart:io` and pty2/xterm deps into the default suite? The file itself has `@TestOn('vm')`. pty_harness.dart imports `package:pty2` and `package:xterm` — these are regular dependencies presumably available in the default suite too (the file compiles fine as the author claims 23/23 green on the default suite). Since `pty_screen_wait_reg_test.dart` also greps... the author says it runs in the default suite and is green locally. Fine.

9. **`waitForRaw` naming**: there's already `waitForText`, `waitForScreen`, `waitForOutput`. `waitForRaw` is consistent. Good.

10. **Test timeout**: the countdown test has `@Timeout(Duration(minutes: 5))`. New wait is 120 s for drain + 60 s for start + 60 s mid-flight + 30 s for 0 running + settle windows... worst case: boot 90 s + 60 + 60 + 120 + 30 + 15 + settle windows. That exceeds 5 minutes? Let's add: waitForBoot (90+15=105 s), waitForScreen allRunning (60), mid-flight loop (60), waitForRaw (120), waitForScreen 0 running (30), waitForOutput settles (0.4+0.2+0.2+0.3 ≈ 1.1 s), exit (15). Total worst ≈ 105+60+60+120+30+1+15 = 391 s ≈ 6.5 min > 5 min timeout. But that's only if EVERYTHING times out at max; and pre-existing waits were: boot 105 + 60 + 60 + 60 (old waitForOutput 60 s) + 30 + 15 = 330 s ≈ 5.5 min — already …

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1345
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1345
- **Title**: test(1337): anchor countdown drain on the settle-notice predicate, not stream silence
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1337-pty-countdown-flake` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +118
- **Deletions**: -17
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T20:00:31Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T20:28:49Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1337

## Root cause (why the window «expired» on the slow runner)

The failing assertion is the settle-set check in `shell_job_countdown_pty_test.dart` (#573 review): expected `{1..10}`, actual `{1..7}` — job 8's settle notice (and 9, 10) missing from the capture. Not a product bug in the job board: `waitForScreen('10 running')` had already passed, so all ten jobs started.

The drained wait was `waitForOutput(settleMs: 500, timeout: 60 s)` — a **silence settle** (returns once the raw buffer is unchanged for 2 consecutive 500 ms polls ≈ 1 s of stream quiet). But this scenario staggers its ten `sleep` jobs **exactly 1 s apart** (3..12 s), so the gaps *between* settle notices sit right on that threshold. One stretched inter-notice gap on the loaded runner (job 7 → 8) satisfied the silence rule and the wait **returned mid-drain** with the tail jobs unlanded — hence exactly `{1..7}`. Aggravator: `waitForOutput` returns silently on timeout, so expiry never surfaced diagnostics; the 60 s ceiling was never even reached.

## Fix shape

1. **Harness primitive** (`pty_harness.dart`): new `FaCliHarness.waitForRaw(matched, {what, timeout})` — the predicate-anchored raw-stream wait, reusing the existing `pollUntil` engine: polls the accumulated raw buffer until `matched` accepts, returns the capture AT the hit, and throws `TimeoutException` with screen + raw-tail diagnostics on expiry. Available to all sibling suites.
2. **Proof predicate extracted** (`settledJobNumbers` + `shellJobSettleNotice`): top-level in the harness (the `maskedValueRow` convention — unit-testable without a PTY), keeping the existing tolerances: DISTINCT-set proof against repaint re-emits, number-prefix match against CI-load mid-id fragmentation (`sh-10-…xqo<esc>… exited(0)`).
3. **Test rewired**: the drained wait is now `waitForRaw((raw) => settledJobNumbers(raw).length == 10, timeout: 120 s)` — anchored on the proof data itself, generous CI ceiling, loud expiry. The screen-side proofs are untouched: `10 running` peak, mid-countdown photo, `0 running` drain, terminal summary card, composer-reserved rows.

## What stays proven

Unchanged contract: all ten background jobs start (board peaks at `10 running`), the count is photographed strictly between 10 and 0, **every one of the ten jobs settles** (distinct settle notices `{1..10}`), the board drains to `0 running · 10 done · 0 lost` with no live row and no foreign paint in the composer's reserved zone.

## Local verification (honest disclosure)

- `dart analyze` clean on the three touched files; **23/23 green** on the harness default-suite unit proofs (`pty_harness_settled_jobs_test` (new: repaint dedup, fragmentation tolerance, truncated-{1..7} rejection), `poll_until`, `masked_value_row`, `frame_content`, `fa_bin`) + the gh-1049 `pty_screen_wait_reg` guard — Dart 3.13.4 temp SDK + fleet pub cache.
- The PTY leg itself **could not run locally**: `PseudoTerminal.start` fails with `openpty failed` on this Mac (the known sibling-lane blocker; deterministic <1 s, unrelated to the scenario). Per repo policy PTY-tagged tests run in nightly + on demand, not the per-PR gate — the green per-PR legs here are the unit proofs above; the integration shard is CI's to prove.
- Deliberately NOT included: a whole-file `dart format` reflow of the countdown suite (formatter version skew would bury the ~40-line fix under 260 lines of churn; no CI format gate on this file).

# pr-1345: test(1337): anchor countdown drain on the settle-notice predicate, not stream silence

## Description

Fixes #1337

## Root cause (why the window «expired» on the slow runner)

The failing assertion is the settle-set check in `shell_job_countdown_pty_test.dart` (#573 review): expected `{1..10}`, actual `{1..7}` — job 8's settle notice (and 9, 10) missing from the capture. Not a product bug in the job board: `waitForScreen('10 running')` had already passed, so all ten jobs started.

The drained wait was `waitForOutput(settleMs: 500, timeout: 60 s)` — a **silence settle** (returns once the raw buffer is unchanged for 2 consecutive 500 ms polls ≈ 1 s of stream quiet). But this scenario staggers its ten `sleep` jobs **exactly 1 s apart** (3..12 s), so the gaps *between* settle notices sit right on that threshold. One stretched inter-notice gap on the loaded runner (job 7 → 8) satisfied the silence rule and the wait **returned mid-drain** with the tail jobs unlanded — hence exactly `{1..7}`. Aggravator: `waitForOutput` returns silently on timeout, so expiry never surfaced diagnostics; the 60 s ceiling was never even reached.

## Fix shape

1. **Harness primitive** (`pty_harness.dart`): new `FaCliHarness.waitForRaw(matched, {what, timeout})` — the predicate-anchored raw-stream wait, reusing the existing `pollUntil` engine: polls the accumulated raw buffer until `matched` accepts, returns the capture AT the hit, and throws `TimeoutException` with screen + raw-tail diagnostics on expiry. Available to all sibling suites.
2. **Proof predicate extracted** (`settledJobNumbers` + `shellJobSettleNotice`): top-level in the harness (the `maskedValueRow` convention — unit-testable without a PTY), keeping the existing tolerances: DISTINCT-set proof against repaint re-emits, number-prefix match against CI-load mid-id fragmentation (`sh-10-…xqo<esc>… exited(0)`).
3. **Test rewired**: the drained wait is now `waitForRaw((raw) => settledJobNumbers(raw).length == 10, timeout: 120 s)` — anchored on the proof data itself, generous CI ceiling, loud expiry. The screen-side proofs are untouched: `10 running` peak, mid-countdown photo, `0 running` drain, terminal summary card, composer-reserved rows.

## What stays proven

Unchanged contract: all ten background jobs start (board peaks at `10 running`), the count is photographed strictly between 10 and 0, **every one of the ten jobs settles** (distinct settle notices `{1..10}`), the board drains to `0 running · 10 done · 0 lost` with no live row and no foreign paint in the composer's reserved zone.

## Local verification (honest disclosure)

- `dart analyze` clean on the three touched files; **23/23 green** on the harness default-suite unit proofs (`pty_harness_settled_jobs_test` (new: repaint dedup, fragmentation tolerance, truncated-{1..7} rejection), `poll_until`, `masked_value_row`, `frame_content`, `fa_bin`) + the gh-1049 `pty_screen_wait_reg` guard — Dart 3.13.4 temp SDK + fleet pub cache.
- The PTY leg itself **could not run locally**: `PseudoTerminal.start` fails with `openpty failed` on this Mac (the known sibling-lane blocker; deterministic <1 s, unrelated to the scenario). Per repo policy PTY-tagged tests run in nightly + on demand, not the per-PR gate — the green per-PR legs here are the unit proofs above; the integration shard is CI's to prove.
- Deliberately NOT included: a whole-file `dart format` reflow of the countdown suite (formatter version skew would bury the ~40-line fix under 260 lines of churn; no CI format gate on this file).

Now I have all three changed files. Let me verify:

1. The diff matches the files on disk (the repo is presumably checked out at the PR HEAD).
2. Run the analysis checks that I can.
3. Consider other suites that used `_settleNotice` — did other tests use the same regex pattern that could now be consolidated? Let me grep for `settleNotice`, `exited(0)`, `waitForOutput(settleMs: 500`, and similar patterns in the repo for potential duplication the PR could have addressed (or duplication introduced).

Key review questions:

1. **Correctness of `waitForRaw`**: it delegates to `pollUntil`, polling `matched(_rawBuffer.toString())` every 50 ms with the timeout. On hit, returns `_rawBuffer.toString()`. Good — capture at hit.

2. **Regex `shellJobSettleNotice = RegExp(r'\[bash\] sh-(\S+) exited\(0\)')`**:
   - `(\S+)` is greedy. For a line like `[bash] sh-10-…xqo<esc>[11;29H5<esc>[11;31H exited(0)`, the `\S+` will match `10-…xqo\x1b[11;29H5\x1b[11;31H` — wait, are escape characters `\S`? `\x1b` (ESC) is a non-whitespace character (it's a control char but not whitespace), so yes `\S+` matches it. Then ` exited(0)` follows. So group(1) = `10-…xqo\x1b[11;29H5\x1b[11;31H`, and `.split('-').first` = `10`. OK, the fragmentation test passes.
   - But what about fragmentation BETWEEN the number and the dash? E.g. if a repaint interleaves an escape after `sh-1` and before `0`, group(1) would be `1\x1b[11;29H0...`. Then `.split('-').first` = `1\x1b[11;29H0` — wait, no. `split('-')` splits on `-`; the first token would be `1\x1b[11;29H0` — hmm, actually if escape is inserted mid-number, split('-').first returns the corrupted number token like `1<ESc>[11;29H0`, which would NOT equal `10`, inflating the distinct set with a corrupt entry. The doc says "The number is the first token written, so it survives any such fragmentation" — that assumes the fragmentation occurs after the full number is written. The observed case (`sh-10-…xqo<esc>[11;29H5<esc>[11;31H`) is mid-id (after the number and first dash). This is a pre-existing tolerance (was in the old test code too), not newly introduced. It's a known limitation documented. Not a regression. Could flag as a suggestion at most — but it's pre-existing behavior moved. Since the code was moved verbatim, this is fine.

   - Another subtlety: what if a settle notice is for a FAILED job, i.e. `exited(1)` or `lost`? The regex only matches `exited\(0\)`. The old regex was the same, so no change. But hmm — the drained wait requires exactly 10 distinct numbers with `exited(0)`. If a job fails (exited(1)), the wait would never satisfy and it'd hit the 120 s timeout, throwing with diagnostics. That's arguably correct behavior (test should fail loudly), fine for a test.

   - What about `\S+` greediness combined with multiple notices one line? E.g. `[bash] sh-1-a exited(0) [bash] sh-2-b exited(0)`. `allMatches` — after the first match consumes `1-a` (greedy `\S+` would try to match as much non-space as possible: `1-a` then ` exited(0)`). Wait — greedy `\S+` matches `1-a`, then requires ` exited\(0\)`. It works. Second match found later. But what if the raw stream contains `[bash] sh-1-a exited(0)[bash] sh-2-b exited(0)` (no space between)? Greedy `\S+` would match `1-a` and then need ` exited(0)` — ` exited(0)` present, matches `1-a`. Fine.

   - What about `exited(0)` for `sh-10-abc10 exited(0)` — greedy `\S+`: could `\S+` match `10-abc10` and then ` exited(0)` — yes. Good.

   - Edge: the number-prefix extraction `m.group(1)!.split('-').first`. If a job id fragment contains a `-` before the number (can't — id always starts `sh-N-...`). OK.

3. **`settledJobNumbers` returning a Set<String> of numbers as strings**: the test expects `{for (var i = 1; i <= 10; i++) '$i'}` — fine.

4. **Potential issue — the `waitForRaw` predicate `settledJobNumbers(raw).length == 10` counts distinct numbers GLOBALLY in the raw buffer, not just for THIS scenario's jobs.** The harness CWD is a unique temp git dir, the session is fresh per spawn, so only this scenario's jobs exist. But `settledJobNumbers` counts ANY `[bash] sh-… exited(0)` notice in the raw buffer. If some earlier part of the scenario (the boot, or the first turn) ran other bash jobs... In this test, the scripted turns only launch the ten sleep jobs. OK. But as a harness-level API (available to all sibling suites), the count-based predicate semantics are the caller's concern. Fine.

5. **The `what:` parameter default and the `timeout` default of 10 s** — consistent with `waitForText`/`waitForScreen` (which use 10 s default). Good.

6. **The `_rawBuffer` access in `waitForRaw` — `_rawBuffer.toString()` is computed on every poll iteration twice (once in matched, once onHit)**. For a long raw buffer (a 2-minute PTY session could accumulate a lot of output), `StringBuffer.toString()` is O(n) each poll — every 50 ms. `waitForText` does the same (`_rawBuffer.toString()` per poll), so consistent with existing patterns. And the predicate `settledJobNumbers(raw)` runs a regex over the entire raw buffer every 50 ms — O(n) per poll. For a 5-minute test with heavy repaints, the raw buffer could be hundreds of KB to a few MB. Running `allMatches` over it every 50 ms = 10k regex scans/s over ~1 MB → could add CPU load on the runner, slightly aggravating the very load the test suffers from. Hmm, this is worth a SUGGESTION: the predicate could track the last-checked length or the regex could be applied only to the tail. But is it a real problem? The raw buffer of a countdown session: ten jobs over ~12 s with a TUI repainting... TUI repaints can be substantial (full-frame repaints, maybe a few KB per frame). Over ~120 s at, say, 5-10 repaints/s * 2-4 KB = maybe 1-4 MB. Regex over 4 MB every 50 ms: `allMatches` with a literal-prefix regex — Dart regex will scan for `[bash] sh-` literal occurrences; ~4 MB scan is on the order of a few ms (simple literal scan is fast, maybe 1-10 ms). So per poll ~ up to 10 ms CPU every 50 ms = up to 20% of one core. Non-trivial but not fatal on a test runner; and `waitForText` already does `.contains(pattern)` per poll which is also O(n). I'll note it as a SUGGESTION (capture last-match-end / incremental scanning), not blocking.

7. **Duplication**: `_settleNotice` in the countdown test was removed and now uses the harness-level `shellJobSettleNotice`/`settledJobNumbers` — good consolidation. Are there OTHER suites that define the same regex locally (`\[bash\] sh-… exited`)? Let me grep. If other suites duplicate this pattern, the PR could have consolidated them too — but that might be scope creep; the ticket scopes to the countdown flake. Still, worth checking for at least flagging as a suggestion (or noting they intentionally left them).

8. **The new test file `pty_harness_settled_jobs_test.dart` runs in the DEFAULT suite** (no integration tag) — it imports `pty_harness.dart`. Does importing pty_harness.dart pull in `dart:io` and pty2/xterm deps into the default suite? The file itself has `@TestOn('vm')`. pty_harness.dart imports `package:pty2` and `package:xterm` — these are regular dependencies presumably available in the default suite too (the file compiles fine as the author claims 23/23 green on the default suite). Since `pty_screen_wait_reg_test.dart` also greps... the author says it runs in the default suite and is green locally. Fine.

9. **`waitForRaw` naming**: there's already `waitForText`, `waitForScreen`, `waitForOutput`. `waitForRaw` is consistent. Good.

10. **Test timeout**: the countdown test has `@Timeout(Duration(minutes: 5))`. New wait is 120 s for drain + 60 s for start + 60 s mid-flight + 30 s for 0 running + settle windows... worst case: boot 90 s + 60 + 60 + 120 + 30 + 15 + settle windows. That exceeds 5 minutes? Let's add: waitForBoot (90+15=105 s), waitForScreen allRunning (60), mid-flight loop (60), waitForRaw (120), waitForScreen 0 running (30), waitForOutput settles (0.4+0.2+0.2+0.3 ≈ 1.1 s), exit (15). Total worst ≈ 105+60+60+120+30+1+15 = 391 s ≈ 6.5 min > 5 min timeout. But that's only if EVERYTHING times out at max; and pre-existing waits were: boot 105 + 60 + 60 + 60 (old waitForOutput 60 s) + 30 + 15 = 330 s ≈ 5.5 min — already …

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1345
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1345
- **Title**: test(1337): anchor countdown drain on the settle-notice predicate, not stream silence
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1337-pty-countdown-flake` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +118
- **Deletions**: -17
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T20:00:31Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T20:28:49Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1337

## Root cause (why the window «expired» on the slow runner)

The failing assertion is the settle-set check in `shell_job_countdown_pty_test.dart` (#573 review): expected `{1..10}`, actual `{1..7}` — job 8's settle notice (and 9, 10) missing from the capture. Not a product bug in the job board: `waitForScreen('10 running')` had already passed, so all ten jobs started.

The drained wait was `waitForOutput(settleMs: 500, timeout: 60 s)` — a **silence settle** (returns once the raw buffer is unchanged for 2 consecutive 500 ms polls ≈ 1 s of stream quiet). But this scenario staggers its ten `sleep` jobs **exactly 1 s apart** (3..12 s), so the gaps *between* settle notices sit right on that threshold. One stretched inter-notice gap on the loaded runner (job 7 → 8) satisfied the silence rule and the wait **returned mid-drain** with the tail jobs unlanded — hence exactly `{1..7}`. Aggravator: `waitForOutput` returns silently on timeout, so expiry never surfaced diagnostics; the 60 s ceiling was never even reached.

## Fix shape

1. **Harness primitive** (`pty_harness.dart`): new `FaCliHarness.waitForRaw(matched, {what, timeout})` — the predicate-anchored raw-stream wait, reusing the existing `pollUntil` engine: polls the accumulated raw buffer until `matched` accepts, returns the capture AT the hit, and throws `TimeoutException` with screen + raw-tail diagnostics on expiry. Available to all sibling suites.
2. **Proof predicate extracted** (`settledJobNumbers` + `shellJobSettleNotice`): top-level in the harness (the `maskedValueRow` convention — unit-testable without a PTY), keeping the existing tolerances: DISTINCT-set proof against repaint re-emits, number-prefix match against CI-load mid-id fragmentation (`sh-10-…xqo<esc>… exited(0)`).
3. **Test rewired**: the drained wait is now `waitForRaw((raw) => settledJobNumbers(raw).length == 10, timeout: 120 s)` — anchored on the proof data itself, generous CI ceiling, loud expiry. The screen-side proofs are untouched: `10 running` peak, mid-countdown photo, `0 running` drain, terminal summary card, composer-reserved rows.

## What stays proven

Unchanged contract: all ten background jobs start (board peaks at `10 running`), the count is photographed strictly between 10 and 0, **every one of the ten jobs settles** (distinct settle notices `{1..10}`), the board drains to `0 running · 10 done · 0 lost` with no live row and no foreign paint in the composer's reserved zone.

## Local verification (honest disclosure)

- `dart analyze` clean on the three touched files; **23/23 green** on the harness default-suite unit proofs (`pty_harness_settled_jobs_test` (new: repaint dedup, fragmentation tolerance, truncated-{1..7} rejection), `poll_until`, `masked_value_row`, `frame_content`, `fa_bin`) + the gh-1049 `pty_screen_wait_reg` guard — Dart 3.13.4 temp SDK + fleet pub cache.
- The PTY leg itself **could not run locally**: `PseudoTerminal.start` fails with `openpty failed` on this Mac (the known sibling-lane blocker; deterministic <1 s, unrelated to the scenario). Per repo policy PTY-tagged tests run in nightly + on demand, not the per-PR gate — the green per-PR legs here are the unit proofs above; the integration shard is CI's to prove.
- Deliberately NOT included: a whole-file `dart format` reflow of the countdown suite (formatter version skew would bury the ~40-line fix under 260 lines of churn; no CI format gate on this file).

Now I have all three changed files. Let me verify:

1. The diff matches the files on disk (the repo is presumably checked out at the PR HEAD).
2. Run the analysis checks that I can.
3. Consider other suites that used `_settleNotice` — did other tests use the same regex pattern that could now be consolidated? Let me grep for `settleNotice`, `exited(0)`, `waitForOutput(settleMs: 500`, and similar patterns in the repo for potential duplication the PR could have addressed (or duplication introduced).

Key review questions:

1. **Correctness of `waitForRaw`**: it delegates to `pollUntil`, polling `matched(_rawBuffer.toString())` every 50 ms with the timeout. On hit, returns `_rawBuffer.toString()`. Good — capture at hit.

2. **Regex `shellJobSettleNotice = RegExp(r'\[bash\] sh-(\S+) exited\(0\)')`**:
   - `(\S+)` is greedy. For a line like `[bash] sh-10-…xqo<esc>[11;29H5<esc>[11;31H exited(0)`, the `\S+` will match `10-…xqo\x1b[11;29H5\x1b[11;31H` — wait, are escape characters `\S`? `\x1b` (ESC) is a non-whitespace character (it's a control char but not whitespace), so yes `\S+` matches it. Then ` exited(0)` follows. So group(1) = `10-…xqo\x1b[11;29H5\x1b[11;31H`, and `.split('-').first` = `10`. OK, the fragmentation test passes.
   - But what about fragmentation BETWEEN the number and the dash? E.g. if a repaint interleaves an escape after `sh-1` and before `0`, group(1) would be `1\x1b[11;29H0...`. Then `.split('-').first` = `1\x1b[11;29H0` — wait, no. `split('-')` splits on `-`; the first token would be `1\x1b[11;29H0` — hmm, actually if escape is inserted mid-number, split('-').first returns the corrupted number token like `1<ESc>[11;29H0`, which would NOT equal `10`, inflating the distinct set with a corrupt entry. The doc says "The number is the first token written, so it survives any such fragmentation" — that assumes the fragmentation occurs after the full number is written. The observed case (`sh-10-…xqo<esc>[11;29H5<esc>[11;31H`) is mid-id (after the number and first dash). This is a pre-existing tolerance (was in the old test code too), not newly introduced. It's a known limitation documented. Not a regression. Could flag as a suggestion at most — but it's pre-existing behavior moved. Since the code was moved verbatim, this is fine.

   - Another subtlety: what if a settle notice is for a FAILED job, i.e. `exited(1)` or `lost`? The regex only matches `exited\(0\)`. The old regex was the same, so no change. But hmm — the drained wait requires exactly 10 distinct numbers with `exited(0)`. If a job fails (exited(1)), the wait would never satisfy and it'd hit the 120 s timeout, throwing with diagnostics. That's arguably correct behavior (test should fail loudly), fine for a test.

   - What about `\S+` greediness combined with multiple notices one line? E.g. `[bash] sh-1-a exited(0) [bash] sh-2-b exited(0)`. `allMatches` — after the first match consumes `1-a` (greedy `\S+` would try to match as much non-space as possible: `1-a` then ` exited(0)`). Wait — greedy `\S+` matches `1-a`, then requires ` exited\(0\)`. It works. Second match found later. But what if the raw stream contains `[bash] sh-1-a exited(0)[bash] sh-2-b exited(0)` (no space between)? Greedy `\S+` would match `1-a` and then need ` exited(0)` — ` exited(0)` present, matches `1-a`. Fine.

   - What about `exited(0)` for `sh-10-abc10 exited(0)` — greedy `\S+`: could `\S+` match `10-abc10` and then ` exited(0)` — yes. Good.

   - Edge: the number-prefix extraction `m.group(1)!.split('-').first`. If a job id fragment contains a `-` before the number (can't — id always starts `sh-N-...`). OK.

3. **`settledJobNumbers` returning a Set<String> of numbers as strings**: the test expects `{for (var i = 1; i <= 10; i++) '$i'}` — fine.

4. **Potential issue — the `waitForRaw` predicate `settledJobNumbers(raw).length == 10` counts distinct numbers GLOBALLY in the raw buffer, not just for THIS scenario's jobs.** The harness CWD is a unique temp git dir, the session is fresh per spawn, so only this scenario's jobs exist. But `settledJobNumbers` counts ANY `[bash] sh-… exited(0)` notice in the raw buffer. If some earlier part of the scenario (the boot, or the first turn) ran other bash jobs... In this test, the scripted turns only launch the ten sleep jobs. OK. But as a harness-level API (available to all sibling suites), the count-based predicate semantics are the caller's concern. Fine.

5. **The `what:` parameter default and the `timeout` default of 10 s** — consistent with `waitForText`/`waitForScreen` (which use 10 s default). Good.

6. **The `_rawBuffer` access in `waitForRaw` — `_rawBuffer.toString()` is computed on every poll iteration twice (once in matched, once onHit)**. For a long raw buffer (a 2-minute PTY session could accumulate a lot of output), `StringBuffer.toString()` is O(n) each poll — every 50 ms. `waitForText` does the same (`_rawBuffer.toString()` per poll), so consistent with existing patterns. And the predicate `settledJobNumbers(raw)` runs a regex over the entire raw buffer every 50 ms — O(n) per poll. For a 5-minute test with heavy repaints, the raw buffer could be hundreds of KB to a few MB. Running `allMatches` over it every 50 ms = 10k regex scans/s over ~1 MB → could add CPU load on the runner, slightly aggravating the very load the test suffers from. Hmm, this is worth a SUGGESTION: the predicate could track the last-checked length or the regex could be applied only to the tail. But is it a real problem? The raw buffer of a countdown session: ten jobs over ~12 s with a TUI repainting... TUI repaints can be substantial (full-frame repaints, maybe a few KB per frame). Over ~120 s at, say, 5-10 repaints/s * 2-4 KB = maybe 1-4 MB. Regex over 4 MB every 50 ms: `allMatches` with a literal-prefix regex — Dart regex will scan for `[bash] sh-` literal occurrences; ~4 MB scan is on the order of a few ms (simple literal scan is fast, maybe 1-10 ms). So per poll ~ up to 10 ms CPU every 50 ms = up to 20% of one core. Non-trivial but not fatal on a test runner; and `waitForText` already does `.contains(pattern)` per poll which is also O(n). I'll note it as a SUGGESTION (capture last-match-end / incremental scanning), not blocking.

7. **Duplication**: `_settleNotice` in the countdown test was removed and now uses the harness-level `shellJobSettleNotice`/`settledJobNumbers` — good consolidation. Are there OTHER suites that define the same regex locally (`\[bash\] sh-… exited`)? Let me grep. If other suites duplicate this pattern, the PR could have consolidated them too — but that might be scope creep; the ticket scopes to the countdown flake. Still, worth checking for at least flagging as a suggestion (or noting they intentionally left them).

8. **The new test file `pty_harness_settled_jobs_test.dart` runs in the DEFAULT suite** (no integration tag) — it imports `pty_harness.dart`. Does importing pty_harness.dart pull in `dart:io` and pty2/xterm deps into the default suite? The file itself has `@TestOn('vm')`. pty_harness.dart imports `package:pty2` and `package:xterm` — these are regular dependencies presumably available in the default suite too (the file compiles fine as the author claims 23/23 green on the default suite). Since `pty_screen_wait_reg_test.dart` also greps... the author says it runs in the default suite and is green locally. Fine.

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1345
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1345
- **Title**: test(1337): anchor countdown drain on the settle-notice predicate, not stream silence
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1337-pty-countdown-flake` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +118
- **Deletions**: -17
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T20:00:31Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T20:28:49Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1337

## Root cause (why the window «expired» on the slow runner)

The failing assertion is the settle-set check in `shell_job_countdown_pty_test.dart` (#573 review): expected `{1..10}`, actual `{1..7}` — job 8's settle notice (and 9, 10) missing from the capture. Not a product bug in the job board: `waitForScreen('10 running')` had already passed, so all ten jobs started.

The drained wait was `waitForOutput(settleMs: 500, timeout: 60 s)` — a **silence settle** (returns once the raw buffer is unchanged for 2 consecutive 500 ms polls ≈ 1 s of stream quiet). But this scenario staggers its ten `sleep` jobs **exactly 1 s apart** (3..12 s), so the gaps *between* settle notices sit right on that threshold. One stretched inter-notice gap on the loaded runner (job 7 → 8) satisfied the silence rule and the wait **returned mid-drain** with the tail jobs unlanded — hence exactly `{1..7}`. Aggravator: `waitForOutput` returns silently on timeout, so expiry never surfaced diagnostics; the 60 s ceiling was never even reached.

## Fix shape

1. **Harness primitive** (`pty_harness.dart`): new `FaCliHarness.waitForRaw(matched, {what, timeout})` — the predicate-anchored raw-stream wait, reusing the existing `pollUntil` engine: polls the accumulated raw buffer until `matched` accepts, returns the capture AT the hit, and throws `TimeoutException` with screen + raw-tail diagnostics on expiry. Available to all sibling suites.
2. **Proof predicate extracted** (`settledJobNumbers` + `shellJobSettleNotice`): top-level in the harness (the `maskedValueRow` convention — unit-testable without a PTY), keeping the existing tolerances: DISTINCT-set proof against repaint re-emits, number-prefix match against CI-load mid-id fragmentation (`sh-10-…xqo<esc>… exited(0)`).
3. **Test rewired**: the drained wait is now `waitForRaw((raw) => settledJobNumbers(raw).length == 10, timeout: 120 s)` — anchored on the proof data itself, generous CI ceiling, loud expiry. The screen-side proofs are untouched: `10 running` peak, mid-countdown photo, `0 running` drain, terminal summary card, composer-reserved rows.

## What stays proven

Unchanged contract: all ten background jobs start (board peaks at `10 running`), the count is photographed strictly between 10 and 0, **every one of the ten jobs settles** (distinct settle notices `{1..10}`), the board drains to `0 running · 10 done · 0 lost` with no live row and no foreign paint in the composer's reserved zone.

## Local verification (honest disclosure)

- `dart analyze` clean on the three touched files; **23/23 green** on the harness default-suite unit proofs (`pty_harness_settled_jobs_test` (new: repaint dedup, fragmentation tolerance, truncated-{1..7} rejection), `poll_until`, `masked_value_row`, `frame_content`, `fa_bin`) + the gh-1049 `pty_screen_wait_reg` guard — Dart 3.13.4 temp SDK + fleet pub cache.
- The PTY leg itself **could not run locally**: `PseudoTerminal.start` fails with `openpty failed` on this Mac (the known sibling-lane blocker; deterministic <1 s, unrelated to the scenario). Per repo policy PTY-tagged tests run in nightly + on demand, not the per-PR gate — the green per-PR legs here are the unit proofs above; the integration shard is CI's to prove.
- Deliberately NOT included: a whole-file `dart format` reflow of the countdown suite (formatter version skew would bury the ~40-line fix under 260 lines of churn; no CI format gate on this file).
